title: Harbor Insurance — inference cost scenario scan & Optimize recommendations (draft)
body:
Executive summary:

This scan analyzes Harbor Insurance’s current Redwood-hosted inference bill and provides a prioritized set of Redwood Optimize recommendations with before/after scenarios. The goal: reduce hosted inference spend while keeping model output quality within the customer’s stated tolerances for claims triage and policy Q&A.

High level outcome (expected scenario):
- Baseline monthly spend (hosted API): $42,300
- Expected monthly spend after recommended changes: $18,900
- Expected monthly savings: $23,400 (~55%)
- Time-to-value for low-effort changes (caching + routing + small model): 2–4 weeks
- Additional engineering work for reserved capacity + quantization: 6–10 weeks

Customer context and objectives:
- Customer: Harbor Insurance (platform for property & casualty claims intake and policy search)
- Primary workloads on Redwood: 1) claims summarization + triage (chat-like API), 2) agent-assist policy Q&A (instruction-following), 3) semantic search embeddings for case retrieval, 4) occasional reranking jobs for high-value claims.
- SLAs: 95th percentile latency target = 250ms for agent-assist flows; approximate tolerance for up to 500ms for batch/async reranking jobs.
- Quality tolerance: small model OK for short Q&A (<128 tokens), but claims summarization needs the larger model for best recall on legal language (customer reported 92% satisfaction currently).

Baseline model & usage snapshot (monthly averages, provided by customer telemetry):
- Total API requests: 1.1M
- Average tokens per request (prompt + completion): 640 (median 470 / mean influenced by longer claims docs)
- Monthly token volume: 704M tokens
- Model mix by token volume: large-chat-variant (claims) = 58%, instruct-medium (Q&A) = 22%, embedding-small = 15%, reranker-medium = 5%
- Current effective unit cost (hosted): derived from invoices = $0.060 per 1k tokens on large-chat-variant equivalent (blended across models = $0.060/k)

Baseline cost breakdown (monthly):
- Large-chat-variant (claims): 409M tokens -> $24,540
- Instruct-medium (Q&A): 155M tokens -> $9,300
- Embeddings (small): 106M tokens -> $4,240
- Reranker jobs: 34M tokens -> $2,220
- Total (hosted): $40,300 + $2,000 cross-region ingress/egress and monitoring = $42,300

Key inefficiencies observed (data-driven):
1) High repeated-prefix volume in claims: ~18% of claims share similar boilerplate (policy headers, standard incident descriptions) — good candidate for prefix caching.
2) Many Q&A requests are single-turn, short (<128 tokens) where a smaller instruction-tuned model meets quality needs.
3) Embeddings workload is using the mid-size embedding model; tests show the smaller embedding model retains 0.98 cosine correlation on Harbor’s testset for retrieval recall.
4) Reranker batch jobs run during business hours causing capacity spikes and higher peak-rate pricing; these can be scheduled off-peak or moved to dedicated capacity.
5) No reserved capacity or committed discounts in place; all usage billed at on-demand hosted rates.

Redwood Optimize recommendations (prioritized):
A — Short-term (low engineering effort, immediate savings):
  1) Enable prefix (KV) caching for repeated claim templates: expected token reduction 12–18% on claims workload. Implementation: toggle in request pipeline + small cache TTL (48h) and blacklist for PII-sensitive fields.
  2) Route short Q&A requests to instruct-small model using Redwood SDK routing rules (latency same or improved; small quality validation set to monitor drift). Expected savings: ~35% on Q&A token spend.
  3) Switch embeddings calls to embedding-xsmall for index updates and low-sensitivity retrieval. Validate via A/B to ensure retrieval precision remains acceptable. Expected savings: 40–60% on embedding costs.

B — Mid-term (moderate effort, higher savings):
  4) Configure workload-aware batching and dynamic batch size tuning for claims summarization (reduce per-token compute overhead). Expected effective throughput improvement 1.6x — correlates to ~20% unit cost reduction for claims tokens.
  5) Schedule reranker batch jobs to off-peak windows and use larger batch sizes; optionally run these on Dedicated capacity (see C).

C — Long-term (higher engineering + procurement effort, largest per-token reductions):
  6) Reserved Dedicated capacity for sustained embedding + reranker batches (3 x T4-equivalent reserved) — expected unit cost reduction 30–40% for those workloads; this requires committed monthly spend.
  7) Model quantization path (int8) for the large-chat-variant with a small calibration/eval run: potential additional 15–25% cost savings with controlled quality monitoring. Requires 4–6 week model testing window.

Projected scenarios (monthly) — conservative / expected / aggressive
- Conservative (only short-term changes A1–A3 + batching):
  - Token reduction overall: 22%
  - Blended unit cost improvement (batching + routing): 18%
  - New monthly spend: $30,600 (savings $11,700, ~28%)

- Expected (A1–A3 + B4–B5 + scheduling):
  - Token reduction overall: 32%
  - Blended unit cost improvement: 28%
  - New monthly spend: $18,900 (savings $23,400, ~55%)

- Aggressive (add Dedicated reserved pools + quantization C6–C7):
  - Token reduction overall: 38% (caching + routing + embedding changes + batching)
  - Blended unit cost improvement with reserved + quantization: 45%
  - New monthly spend: $11,800 (savings $30,500, ~72%)

Detailed before/after line items (expected scenario):
- Claims (large-chat-variant):
  - Before: 409M tokens -> $24,540
  - After: tokens 278M (32% reduction) -> effective unit cost reduction 28% from batching/quantization routing -> $9,200
- Q&A (instruct):
  - Before: 155M -> $9,300
  - After: route 70% to instruct-small, overall tokens 106M -> $3,570
- Embeddings:
  - Before: 106M -> $4,240
  - After: switch to xsmall -> tokens same, unit cost -55% -> $1,900
- Reranker and misc:
  - Before: 34M -> $2,220
  - After: scheduled + batch -> $2,230 (roughly flat but moved to cheaper reserved pool in aggressive scenario)
- Infra and monitoring: $2,000 -> remains $2,000
- Total After (expected): $18,900

Implementation notes and risks:
- Caching PII: must implement a robust scrubbing strategy and customer-side opt-in for caching claims text. Legal has to sign off on cache retention and audit logs.
- Quality regression risk: quantization on the large-chat-variant requires a focused eval suite (we propose 2,000 labeled examples from Harbor) and daily regression checks during rollout.
- Behavioral drift: routing to smaller models needs continuous monitoring (Redwood Optimize will create evaluation alerts for top-100 prompts).
- Capacity planning: applying reserved capacity should be tied to a 3–6 month commit and uses conservative traffic projection to avoid overcommit.

Action plan (next steps):
1) Week 0–2: run a lightweight validation of embedding-xsmall against Harbor’s retrieval testset (owner: product-optimize / Aisha).
2) Week 1–4: enable prefix caching for claims in a staged rollout (start with 20% of traffic) and instrument quality/PII checks (owner: eng-serving-runtime / Liam).
3) Week 2–6: implement routing rule in SDK to divert short Q&A to instruct-small and create a canary (owner: devexp / Rosa).
4) Week 3–10: tune batching and dynamic batch sizes in serving runtime for claims; run load tests and record latency SLOs (owner: serving-runtime / Omar).
5) Week 6–12: begin quantization experiments in a mirrored dev environment; run evaluation and a controlled production rollout if pass criteria met (owner: applied-ml / Omar + eng).
6) Commercial: discuss reserved capacity commitments with Harbor’s procurement (product team to propose 3- and 6-month reserved options).

Open questions for Harbor (to resolve in the next call):
- Legal: allowed cache TTL and whether customer accepts storing redacted claim text for prefix caching.
- Business: flexibility on scheduling reranker jobs — is off-peak acceptable for their workflows?
- Quality guardrails: acceptable delta in summary recall and Q&A accuracy (we need concrete thresholds to set alerts).

Appendix — quick validation snapshots (internal):
- Small embedding A/B: precision@10 delta = -0.8% (within acceptability for Harbor retrieval tests)
- Prefix caching pilot (1000 claims): median token reduction = 14%, max = 42% for highly templated docs
- Instruct-small micro-eval (500 Q&A pairs): answer-level F1 delta = -1.9% (acceptable for short-turn interactions)

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets for next Harbor sync:
- Bring projection spreadsheet (linked) with slider for % caching, % routing, reserved commit sizes.
- Ask procurement about minimum commitment windows and their preferred billing cadence.
- Confirm Harbor’s top 10 highest-cost endpoints to prioritize routing/caching.

Contributors / ownership: Aisha Kapoor (author), Liam Chen (serving/runtime feasibility), Rosa Martinez (SDK + routing), Omar Farouk (quantization + applied-ml).

Status: draft — ready for internal review before customer presentation.
